title: Table 3: mechanism controls on seeds 0-4, with the latent-selector rows

conventions.fold_combination: within-seed: mean of fold AUCs; retrieval hits pooled over folds
conventions.difference: paired by seed, then mean and sample SD of the per-seed differences
conventions.ood_interval: saved 95% paired query bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 0

caption:
\textbf{Candidate directions, intervention operators, and erasure extent.}
E5-small results on three-class SwiLTra and SCOTUS (mean $\pm$ sample SD, seeds 0--4). AUCs are held-out macro one-vs-rest probe scores; R@10 measures paired retrieval. Random SAE selection (row A2) draws uniformly from the same latents that MI scores (training firing rate in $[0.02, 0.98]$; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_A3}). Row A4 uses the smallest number of random non-SAE directions whose Directions-LEACE map reaches or exceeds row A1's normalized squared training displacement ($N$: SwiLTra 40--43; SCOTUS 40--41). The random rows average five draws per seed. Rows A5--A8 rank the same eligible latents without $k$-means: by the entropy of a latent's firing indicator, by Hartigan's dip statistic of the training coordinates along its decoder direction, and by its mean firing mutual information with the other eligible latents (all pairs; negatively correlated pairs only). The oracle (row A9) ranks by mutual information with the true classes: a post hoc reference, not a label-free method. Row B3 is row B2 with the training mean restored, and row B4 removes orthogonally the subspace that Directions-LEACE displaces, $\mathrm{span}(\Sigma D_S^{\top})$, also with the mean restored. Displacement-matched PCA (row C1) removes the fewest principal directions whose training displacement reaches that of row A1 (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_A4}; ranks: SwiLTra 22--23; SCOTUS 22); this matches displacement, not rank or total-variance reduction, and Table~\ref{tab:erasure-extent} repeats the comparison on six settings. The SAEs of this table were fitted separately from those of Table~\ref{tab:primary-id}, and those of the rows marked $\dagger$ separately again (same recipe, seeds and splits throughout); row A1$^{\dagger}$ is row A1 on the latter fits, the baseline for rows A5--A9. The reference rows are the runs of Table~\ref{tab:primary-id}.
notes: Decision 5 of 2026-10-07: the selector rows are merged as they are. Row A1 on the selector study's fits is printed as row A1 (dagger): swiltra_de_fr_it 0.6168 (row A1: 0.6157); scotus_oyez_lexis_wiki 0.7371 (row A1: 0.7266)

Reference rows: Table 2's runs are printed. Audited again in the Table 3 runs they differ per seed by at most swiltra_de_fr_it metadata_leace linear_auc: 0.0001; swiltra_de_fr_it metadata_leace mlp_auc: 0.0046; scotus_oyez_lexis_wiki metadata_leace linear_auc: 0.0008; scotus_oyez_lexis_wiki metadata_leace mlp_auc: 0.0015 (Raw: identical). The Metadata-LEACE map is refitted there, and the seeded MLP probe is sensitive to its float32 rounding.
